Ostrander Gull.narrative: I mended nets on this quay before the lower quay was taken, and I still mend them now, though my hands are slower and the twine costs more than it did. I no longer go out; Wick's boat is his, and I watch it come in from the steps. Every name the Surge took is written in my head as well as on Ostrander Sallow's list, and I read it over when the tide lanterns are lit. Kettlebridge sold us stone at a price that would have built the wall twice over, and I do not forget it.
values: a net mended is a boat saved
the quay owes nothing to those who never shared a boat
goals: see the tide lanterns lit for every name on the list
keep Wick's boat in nets and out of debt
see a seawall built before another surge takes the rest of the lower quay
learn to splice the new tarred twine as well as I once did the old
sit with Ostrander Sallow over a pot of fish stew and trade stories of the quay before the Surge
Ostrander Gull.mood: quiet, weathered, slow to anger but slow to forgive

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: My brother's boy. He fishes the harbour mouth like his father did, and I mend his nets for nothing.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: niece by marriage
relations.note: A good cook and a hard worker. She feeds the night crews and never asks a mark of me.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: great-niece
relations.note: A little thing, afraid of the dark water. I tell her the lanterns keep it back.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: customer
relations.note: He pays on time for his nets, which is more than most. A hard man but a fair one.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: fellow keeper
relations.note: We keep the tide lantern list between us. He writes the names; I remember the boats.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She lost her brother as I lost mine. She wants the wall; I want it too, but I doubt she will get the stone.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: chandler
relations.note: His rope and tar are good, but he never forgets a mark owed.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: stone-seller
relations.note: He sold us stone at a price that would have built the wall twice. I do not care what his reasons were.

relations.name: Wick Brine
relations.label: night guard
relations.note: He walks the road at night and knows the smugglers' paths. A useful man to have about the quay.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: builder
relations.note: Patches the lower quay with salvage and wants proper stone; a good lad with a bad job.

relations.name: Rennick Vane
relations.label: quay guard
relations.note: Walks the road with the runners; I'd trust him with a net or a name.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: Her noodle stall has fed me many a cold night; her boy Kai is another matter.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: deserter
relations.note: Went off and left the quay guard; I do not hold with a man who runs.

memories.gist: The night the Surge came, I stood on the upper steps and watched the lower quay go under, and counted the boats that did not come back.
My brother Gull taught me to mend a net before I could row, and I have mended them every day since.
When Wick's father drowned, I took the boy on the steps and showed him how to hold a needle, because there was nothing else I could give him.
Ostrander Sallow and I sat up one winter night writing the drowned list fair, and I named every boat I could remember for him to write.
I went up the fish road once to Kettlebridge to ask about stone, and came back with nothing but a price I could not pay.

stances.why: Every name on the tide lantern list is a boat I knew and a person the quay lost.
The quay's way: you owe nothing to anyone who has not shared a boat with you.
The wall is unbuilt because their stone is dear, and the lower quay stays broken.
A mended net saves a boat; talk saves nothing.
A light lit late is a boat lost. I have seen it.

pastimes: mending nets on the quay steps, one knot at a time
watching Wick's boat come in from the harbour steps
reading over the list of the drowned when the tide lanterns are lit
Ostrander Gull.calling: I mend nets, and a net mended is a boat saved.
